name: game-analytics-pipeline

ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized Access to Game Analytics Data via API Gateway

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers might attempt to forge Cognito tokens, exploit token validation bugs, or use stolen credentials to gain unauthorized access to the API endpoints.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker obtains valid credentials through phishing or token theft, then uses these to submit falsified game analytics data that could skew business metrics or game balance decisions.

recommendations.description: Implement mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for API Gateway endpoints
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure ACM certificates for API Gateway custom domain and enable mutual TLS authentication for client certificate validation.

recommendations.description: Enhance Cognito user pool security settings
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable advanced security features in Cognito user pool, implement MFA, and configure strict password policies.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: API Gateway supports custom authorizers and AWS WAF integration for additional security layers. Consider implementing rate limiting and AWS WAF rules to prevent brute force attacks.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Misconfigured bucket policies, overly permissive IAM roles, or accidentally disabled block public access settings could expose sensitive game analytics data.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker discovers a misconfigured S3 bucket policy that allows listing of objects, downloads sensitive game analytics data, and uses it for competitive analysis or to expose player behavior patterns.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Add a data transformation component in the Lambda processing function to anonymize sensitive player data before storage in processed data bucket.
Enable S3 Block Public Access at account level, implement bucket key encryption, enable versioning, and configure access logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Macie for sensitive data discovery and S3 Block Public Access at the account level. Consider implementing S3 Object Lock for critical data.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Insufficient encryption of data in transit or overly permissive IAM policies could allow unauthorized access to real-time game analytics data streams.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with access to the AWS network infrastructure could potentially intercept or modify game analytics data as it flows between services.

recommendations.description: Enable encryption for all Kinesis streams
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure server-side encryption using KMS for Kinesis Data Streams, Firehose, and Analytics applications.

recommendations.description: Implement strict IAM policies for Kinesis access
recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and restrict IAM roles to minimum required permissions, implement resource-based policies where applicable.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS KMS customer managed keys for Kinesis encryption and implement VPC endpoints for secure access to Kinesis services.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit vulnerabilities in EMR applications, misconfigured security groups, or weak SSH access controls to gain unauthorized access to the cluster.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker gains access to the EMR cluster through a misconfigured security group, then uses this access to manipulate data processing jobs or access sensitive data.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure security groups, use private subnets, enable encryption, and implement proper key management for EMR clusters.
Enable detailed logging, configure CloudWatch alerts, and implement automated security scanning for EMR clusters.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use EMR security configurations to enable encryption and Kerberos authentication. Consider implementing EMR steps using the principle of least privilege.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies or vulnerabilities in the processing Lambda to manipulate game state data in DynamoDB.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker compromises the processing Lambda function and uses its permissions to modify game state data, potentially affecting game balance or player progress.

recommendations.description: Implement strict access controls for DynamoDB
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use fine-grained IAM policies, implement condition keys, and enable DynamoDB encryption at rest.
Enable point-in-time recovery, implement DAX encryption, and configure CloudWatch monitoring for suspicious activity.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use DynamoDB encryption at rest with AWS KMS and implement VPC endpoints for secure access. Consider using DynamoDB Streams for audit logging.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Insufficient data anonymization or access controls in analytics systems could expose sensitive player behavior patterns and personal information.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An analyst with QuickSight access exports detailed player behavior data containing personally identifiable information, leading to privacy violations.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Develop and implement data anonymization processes in the analytics pipeline, focusing on removing or obscuring personally identifiable information.
Implement row-level security in Athena and QuickSight, restrict dataset access, and enable comprehensive audit logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use Lake Formation for fine-grained access control to Athena queries and implement QuickSight row-level security for data access control.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
AWS Serverless Analytics Pipeline Architecture Diagram
This script generates a high-resolution diagram of a modular, serverless analytics
pipeline for game telemetry data using the diagrams package.
"""

# Standard library imports
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge

# Generic nodes for external entities
from diagrams.generic.device import Mobile
from diagrams.generic.compute import Rack
from diagrams.onprem.client import Users

# AWS Analytics imports
from diagrams.aws.analytics import (
    KinesisDataAnalytics,
    KinesisDataFirehose,
    KinesisDataStreams,
    Athena,
    Quicksight,
    EMR
)

# AWS Compute imports
from diagrams.aws.compute import (
    Lambda,
    LambdaFunction
)

# AWS Database imports
from diagrams.aws.database import (
    Dynamodb,
    DynamodbTable
)

# AWS Integration imports
from diagrams.aws.integration import (
    Eventbridge
)

# AWS Network imports
from diagrams.aws.network import (
    APIGateway
)

# AWS Security imports
from diagrams.aws.security import (
    Cognito,
    IAM
)

# AWS Storage imports
from diagrams.aws.storage import (
    S3
)

# AWS Management imports
from diagrams.aws.management import (
    Cloudwatch
)

# Diagram configuration
DIAGRAM_ATTRS = {
    "splines": "ortho",  # Use orthogonal lines for cleaner appearance
    "nodesep": "1.0",    # Increase spacing between nodes
    "ranksep": "1.0",    # Increase spacing between ranks
    "pad": "2.0"         # Add padding around the diagram
}

def create_analytics_pipeline():
    """
    Creates a comprehensive AWS architecture diagram for the serverless
    analytics pipeline, showing data flow from game clients through
    processing and analytics stages.
    """
    
    # Create the main diagram with custom attributes
    with Diagram(
        name="Game Analytics Pipeline Architecture",
        filename="game_analytics_pipeline",
        direction="LR",
        show=True,
        graph_attr=DIAGRAM_ATTRS,
        outformat="png"
    ):
        # Define edge styles
        data_flow = Edge(color="blue", style="bold")
        event_flow = Edge(color="green", style="dashed")
        trust_flow = Edge(color="red", style="dotted")
        
        # Create external data producers cluster
        with Cluster("Data Producers\n(External Zone)"):
            game_clients = Mobile("Game Clients")
            backend_services = Rack("Backend Services")
            
        # Create data consumers cluster
        with Cluster("Data Consumers\n(External Zone)"):
            analysts = Users("Data Analysts")
            developers = Users("Game Developers")
            
        # Create authentication cluster
        with Cluster("Authentication"):
            auth = Cognito("User Authentication")
            
        # Create ingestion cluster
        with Cluster("Data Ingestion"):
            api = APIGateway("API Gateway")
            stream = KinesisDataStreams("Real-time Stream")
            firehose = KinesisDataFirehose("Data Firehose")
        
        # Create processing cluster
        with Cluster("Data Processing"):
            process_lambda = Lambda("Processing Function")
            analytics = KinesisDataAnalytics("Stream Analytics")
            emr = EMR("EMR Processing")
        
        # Create storage cluster
        with Cluster("Data Storage"):
            raw_bucket = S3("Raw Data")
            processed_bucket = S3("Processed Data")
            dynamo = Dynamodb("Game State")
        
        # Create analytics cluster
        with Cluster("Analytics & Visualization"):
            athena = Athena("Data Query")
            quicksight = Quicksight("Dashboards")
        
        # Create monitoring cluster
        with Cluster("Monitoring"):
            events = Eventbridge("Events")
            logs = Cloudwatch("Logs & Metrics")
        
        # Define data flow
        # Producer flows
        [game_clients, backend_services] >> trust_flow >> auth
        auth >> data_flow >> api
        api >> data_flow >> stream
        stream >> data_flow >> [process_lambda, analytics]
        stream >> data_flow >> firehose
        firehose >> data_flow >> raw_bucket
        
        # Processing flows
        process_lambda >> data_flow >> [processed_bucket, dynamo]
        analytics >> data_flow >> processed_bucket
        emr >> data_flow >> processed_bucket
        
        # Analytics flows
        raw_bucket >> data_flow >> emr
        processed_bucket >> data_flow >> athena
        athena >> data_flow >> quicksight
        
        # Consumer flows
        quicksight >> trust_flow >> [analysts, developers]
        dynamo >> trust_flow >> developers
        
        # Event flow
        [process_lambda, analytics, emr] >> event_flow >> events
        events >> event_flow >> logs

if __name__ == "__main__":
    create_analytics_pipeline()
